changeSet.author: osmontero
changeSet.comment:
Migrate every bare utm.X visualization aggregation field to its inferred utm.X.keyword sub-field. Per the standardized-mapping directive, utm.* is the ONLY bag left to OpenSearch inference: the grok parser plugin writes each value as a string, so inference maps it text + .keyword (exactly like the other standardized strings such as action and origin.user, which are already aggregated via .keyword). A terms aggregation on the bare text field fails with search_phase_execution_exception (text has no fielddata) and the backend returns 500 - e.g. dashboard 13 (o365-overview), viz "O365 Top 5 events by Source" bucketing utm.Workload.
This closes the cross-generation drift the directive eliminates: v11.3.0 retro-pinned utm.* to bare keyword (commit 0a6303a228) while v11.2.x indices inferred text+.keyword, so no single utm.X field string aggregated on BOTH generations. utm.X.keyword is the one form valid on every generation: - inferred (text+.keyword) indices: utm.X.keyword returns data; - legacy bare-keyword utm indices: utm.X.keyword is absent and a terms agg on it returns empty (not an error) until the index reindexes/rolls off; - fresh indices under the corrected template: utm.* infers text+.keyword, so utm.X.keyword returns data.
EXCEPTION: utm.responseElements.credentials.expiration is left bare. Its value is an ISO-8601 timestamp OpenSearch date-detects to type date, which has no .keyword sub-field; a bare date field IS aggregatable, so pointing it at .keyword would drop it.
The rewrite is a chained REPLACE over the FULLY-QUOTED field-value token "utm.X" -> "utm.X.keyword". Working on text (not jsonb) preserves the surrounding JSON byte-for-byte. Each token is quoted so only the exact field value is touched (customLabel / name values are unaffected). Idempotent: after the rewrite the bare quoted token "utm.X" no longer exists (it is now "utm.X.keyword"), so a re-run matches nothing.
